title: Target alignment, dilution and forecast selection when cross-sectional forecasts share a common target
abstract: arXiv:2609.26303v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Forecasters often score the same units per date against one standardized realized outcome. We show that every standardized forecast splits exactly into a component aligned with this common target and a component uncorrelated with it. Three consequences follow: forecast-error correlation largely mirrors forecast correlation and is therefore a poor measure of diversity; an equally weighted combination beats a no-information forecast only when average alignment is large relative to the combination's dispersion; and the gain from adding a forecaster separates into genuine improvement and mere dilution, which equal-weight admission can mistakenly reward. We develop a cautious selection rule, study it in simulations, and apply it to language-model forecasts of US equity rankings and mechanical signals ranking exchange-traded funds. Selection removes most dilution losses, but no combination beats the no-information forecast.

translated_title: 当横截面预测共享共同目标时的目标对齐、稀释与预测选择
translated_abstract: 预测者通常针对每个日期的相同单位，用一个标准化的已实现结果进行评分。我们证明，每个标准化预测都可以精确地分解为与该共同目标对齐的成分和与之不相关的成分。由此得出三个结论：预测误差相关性在很大程度上只是反映预测相关性，因此是衡量多样性的一种糟糕指标；等权重组合只有在平均对齐程度相对于组合离散度足够大时，才能胜过无信息预测；添加一个预测者所带来的收益可以分为真正的改进和单纯的稀释，而等权重纳入可能会错误地奖励稀释。我们开发了一个谨慎的选择规则，在模拟中对其进行研究，并将其应用于美国股票排名的语言模型预测以及排名交易所交易基金的机械信号。选择规则消除了大部分稀释损失，但没有任何组合能够胜过无信息预测。
tldr: 该论文证明标准化预测可精确分解为与共同目标对齐的成分和不相关成分，据此揭示预测误差相关性不能有效衡量多样性、等权组合仅在平均对齐度足够高时才优于无信息预测、等权纳入可能错误奖励稀释而非真正改进，并提出一个谨慎的预测者选择规则以消除大部分稀释损失。
en_tdlr: This paper proves that standardized forecasts split exactly into a common-target-aligned component and an uncorrelated one, showing that forecast-error correlation is a poor diversity measure, equal-weight combinations beat no-information forecasts only when average alignment is large relative to dispersion, and equal-weight admission can mistakenly reward mere dilution, for which the authors develop a cautious selection rule that removes most dilution losses.
